en: A single lightning bolt can heat the surrounding air to 30,000 degrees Celsius, which is five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
A single handful of healthy soil contains more microscopic living organisms than the total number of people currently alive on planet Earth.
Pumice is the only rock in the world that naturally floats on water because it is filled with tiny, trapped air bubbles.
If all the water on Earth were gathered into a single sphere, it would be about 1,385 kilometers wide, which is smaller than our Moon.
Venus rotates in the opposite direction of most planets, meaning the sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
A single teaspoon of material from a dense neutron star would weigh about six billion tons on Earth.
The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth at a rate of 3.8 centimeters per year, roughly the speed human fingernails grow.
In the deep ocean, a tsunami wave can travel as fast as a commercial jet airplane, reaching speeds up to 800 kilometers per hour.
The loudest sound in recorded history was the 1883 eruption of the Krakatoa volcano, which was heard clearly 4,800 kilometers away.
Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a massive, swirling storm that has been raging for over 300 years and is wider than planet Earth.
Despite temperatures reaching 5,400 degrees Celsius, Earth's inner core remains solid iron because of the immense, crushing pressure from the layers above it.
A single mature hurricane releases heat energy equivalent to a 10-megaton nuclear bomb exploding every twenty minutes.
